name: Andre Petroski
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: A 35-year-old Renzo Gracie Philly grappler (13-6, 8-5 UFC) who built an 8-2 UFC start on takedowns and long top control, but has now lost three straight, the last two by knockout. Wins by grinding; loses when someone lands clean on him.

how_they_fight.Striking: Functional at best: about 2.9 significant strikes landed a minute against 3.8 absorbed. Uses calf kicks and pressure mainly to set up level changes (Cageside Press, Sherdog on the Brundage fight). Out-struck at range by Edmen Shahbazyan over 15 minutes (34-53 in our data).
how_they_fight.Grappling: The engine of every win: about 2.4 takedowns per 15 minutes, 48% accuracy, and huge control numbers in his decision wins (12:50 of control vs Josh Fremd, 9:20 vs Dylan Budka, 8:00 vs Wellington Turman). Works elbows from side control, looks for cradles and mount (R1 vs Brundage). Submitted Yaozong Hu and Nick Maximov in the UFC. Against a better grappler (Rodolfo Vieira) he kept it standing and won 55-58 on strikes by decision, so he can adapt.
how_they_fight.Defense: Takedown defense is good (~79%), but the chin and the entry are the problem. Five of his six losses are KO/TKOs and three of the last four losses came from a single clean shot as he closed distance or exchanged: Michel Pereira (R1, 1:06), Cam Rowston (counter left hook on his entry, R1 2:41) and Cody Brundage (left hook after a feint, R2 0:44). Also knocked down by Shahbazyan in the decision loss.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Slow burner. Of his 13 wins, five are decisions; two of his three UFC finishes came in R3 (Micheal Gillmore TKO R3, Yaozong Hu SUB R3 at 4:46). Career finishes: R1 4, R2 2, R3 2. His losses come early: KO/TKO losses in R1 (Pereira, Rowston) and R2 (Aaron Jeffery, Jacob Malkoun 0:39, Brundage 0:44); his only decision loss went the distance. He doesn't fade; he gets caught before his grinding pays off. Won R1 on all three Sherdog cards vs Brundage and was stopped 44 seconds into R2.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Knows his path (take it down, ride, elbow) and stuck to it in the win streak. Adapted against a BJJ ace in Vieira. His entries, though, have become predictable and he keeps walking into counters.

patterns: Grinds decisions with takedowns and long top control (5 of his 8 UFC wins went the distance)
UFC finishes came late: R3 TKO and R3 submission; R1 sub of Maximov the exception
Stopped early: all five KO/TKO losses in R1 or the first minute of R2 (Malkoun 0:39, Brundage 0:44)
Three straight losses (Shahbazyan dec, Rowston R1 TKO, Brundage R2 TKO); two straight knockouts
concerns: Durability: KO'd in three of his last four losses and dropped in the fourth
Age 35, three-fight skid; LowKick noted he went 8-2 to start his UFC run and then lost three straight
Opponent Azamat Bekoev is also on a two-fight skid, so both men's jobs may be on the line
keys_to_beat: Counter his entries: he telegraphs the level change behind calf kicks and pressure
Hurt him early; he's never been stopped late
Stay off the fence and get up fast; don't concede the long top-control rounds that win him decisions

news.text: Booked against Azamat Bekoev (20-5) at middleweight for Oct. 31; Rotowire notes Petroski is on a three-fight skid and Bekoev on a two-fight skid.
Lost to Cody Brundage by R2 TKO (0:44) after winning R1 with a takedown and mount; dropped by a left hook after a feint (Sherdog, Cageside Press).
